text:
Maria (Support): customer reports intermittent 401s from an Electron webview. screenshots show the HTTP status but no trace/req id. they said it happens ~10% of calls. can we get a minimal repro ask?

Jon (Eng): first ask: which SDK version / release channel? electron SDK v3+ had a header rename recently.

Maria (Support): electron SDK 3.2.1, using embedded webview, corporate proxy in front. auth token shows valid in their logs.

Alex (SRE): ok. two quick things to request from the customer (minimal, non-blocking):
1) a single successful and single failing request captured as a cURL (from devtools) - see example below.
2) proxy/server access logs around the timestamp (±30s) or the access log lines that match the request (we're looking for any header like X-Redwood-Request-Id / X-Request-Id / x-rw-req that we can correlate).

Alex (SRE): Devtools -> Network -> find the request -> right click -> Copy -> Copy as cURL. They should redact the Authorization header before sending. Example minimal curl to attach:

```
# replace values, then paste here
curl 'https://api.redwood.infer/v1/generate' 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
  -H 'X-Client-Platform: electron-webview' 
  -H 'X-Redwood-Request-Id: <PASTE-HEADER-FROM-PROXY-IF-ANY>' 
  --data-raw '{"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"hello world"}'
```

Alex (SRE): If they can't copy as cURL, a HAR file works too (Export -> Save as HAR). Instruct them to:
- remove sensitive headers (Authorization) or replace with <REDACTED>
- include the failing request entry and the surrounding entries for context

Jon (Eng): for server/proxy logs you can give them a grep snippet they can run: 

```
# search access log for timeframe, adjust path/time as needed
TZ=UTC; grep "2025-02-12T11:22" /var/log/proxy/access.log | egrep -i "redwood|x-request-id|x-redwood|reqid" -A2 -B2
```

Jon (Eng): in our backend we look for either X-Redwood-Request-Id or X-Request-Id. If the proxy strips headers, ask them to paste the complete request line + response status from the proxy logs so we can correlate by timestamp + client IP.

Maria (Support): also include the client-side console log snippet around the failed request (timestamp + SDK version). a one-line stack or network error helps.

TraceBot: automated check: scanned last 24h for errors from that org, found 3 401s at 2025-02-12T11:21:13Z, 2025-02-12T11:23:01Z, 2025-02-12T11:27:45Z. No attached X-Redwood-Request-Id header in those traces.

Alex (SRE): if they can run the curl repro for us, ask them to run it twice (one that fails, one that succeeds) and paste both responses (status line + headers). if we have the full response headers we can see if an auth gateway is rewriting or stripping.

Maria (Support): copy to customer message (short checklist):
- SDK version (3.2.1) + platform (macOS/Windows)
- One failing request as cURL (Copy as cURL) with Authorization redacted
- A matching successful request as cURL if possible
- HAR export if cURL isn't available (only include the failing request entry)
- Proxy/server access log lines for ±30s around the failure timestamps (redact IPs if required)
- Client console/snippet with timestamp and SDK version

Jon (Eng): if they can't share logs, ask for exact ISO timestamps, route path (`/v1/generate`) and client IP so we can search from our side.

Maria (Support): I'll send. once they attach curl/HAR and proxy log snippet we'll escalate to eng with the artifacts. thanks! :thumbsup:
